red.focus: Recognize how bad research harms people
red.summary: A mistaken citation or overlooked deadline is not a harmless academic error. Learn why legal accuracy and careful fact handling protect a client's life, money, and freedom.
checklist: I can identify a research error that could change legal advice
I can verify key citations before writing
I can distinguish accuracy from an impressive bibliography

sections.title: The Cost of a Wrong Rule
sections.body_md: Suppose counsel tells a tenant that a notice period is thirty days based on an outdated webpage. The governing statute now requires a shorter action deadline, and the client loses a chance to challenge eviction. The problem began with source verification, not with elegant writing. A wrong legal proposition can cause concrete harm even when presented in confident prose. The researcher must check current primary law and relevant dates before giving advice about a decision that cannot easily be reversed.

sections.title: A Citation Is a Promise
sections.body_md: When a memorandum cites a case for a legal rule, it implicitly tells the reader that the source exists and supports the proposition. A citation to an unrelated passage, an overruled decision, or a nonexistent case breaks that promise. Verification means opening the authority, reading the relevant text, checking its status and placing it in context. More citations do not repair a false central statement. Good legal writing values a few accurate controlling sources over a display of unverified references.

sections.title: Protect the Client's Account
sections.body_md: Research errors can also arise from misunderstanding facts. Misstating a medical history, filing date or employment event may change the legal rule's application. Separate the client's account from independently verified records and ask about uncertainty without blaming the person. This combination of diligence and respectful listening is crucial when legal work concerns trauma, poverty or loss of liberty. The lawyer's job is to make the information more reliable, not to make the client sound more certain than they are.

yellow.focus: Audit claims and sources for preventable mistakes
yellow.summary: Develop a structured error-checking routine for legal memoranda. Verify not just the existence of authority but the proposition, quotation, procedural context, and remedy it actually supports.
checklist: I can conduct a proposition-to-source audit
I can identify selective quotation and false paraphrase
I can check material deadlines and adverse authority

sections.title: Match the Claim to the Source
sections.body_md: A legal memo states that a case requires proof of intent, but the opinion actually discusses negligence. The citation exists, yet the legal proposition is wrong. Review each material sentence and ask which source supports it, where, and under what conditions. A reliable audit checks the jurisdiction, holding, procedural posture, later treatment and any statutory changes. The purpose is not to punish drafts. It is to prevent a client's decision from resting on a confident but false statement.
sections.audio_script: A legal memo states that a case requires proof of intent, but the opinion actually discusses negligence. The citation exists, yet the legal proposition is wrong. Review each material sentence and ask which source supports it, where, and under what conditions. A reliable audit checks the jurisdiction, holding, procedural posture, later treatment and any statutory changes. The purpose is not to punish drafts. It is to prevent a client's decision from resting on a confident but false statement.

sections.title: Quotes Need Their Surroundings
sections.body_md: A court may say, 'This action is generally unavailable,' and then explain a statutory exception. Quoting only the first clause can mislead as much as inventing a rule. Read enough context to preserve qualifications, dissent versus majority, and whether the statement is binding or incidental. Good paraphrasing reflects what the source actually decided, not merely what an advocate wishes it had said. If the meaning is uncertain, state that limitation rather than silently choosing the broadest interpretation.

sections.title: Prioritize Consequential Checks
sections.body_md: Not every sentence deserves equal audit time. Legal deadlines, jurisdiction, key elements, defenses, adverse authority and requested relief can change whether a case succeeds at all. Check these first, then verify supporting background propositions. Keep a short log of corrections so another reviewer can see what changed. This risk-based method protects clients while respecting the need for concise, efficient work.

orange.focus: Evaluate evidence provenance and research bias
orange.summary: Advanced research requires tracking how factual claims and legal sources entered the record. Learn to investigate missing documents, unreliable databases, and one-sided selection without overclaiming causation.
checklist: I can trace a factual assertion to an identifiable record
I can identify data gaps and provenance risks
I can challenge a favored legal conclusion with adverse evidence

sections.title: Provenance Makes Evidence Inspectable
sections.body_md: A spreadsheet summarizing thousands of transactions may appear convincing, but the researcher should know who collected the figures, from what system, and with what exclusions. Records can be altered, deduplicated incorrectly or stripped of context. Legal admissibility and weight remain separate inquiries governed by the tribunal's rules. A responsible memo describes the data source, transformations and limits before inferring wrongdoing. This is especially important when a single analysis may affect many employees, patients or customers.

sections.title: Databases Contain Selection Effects
sections.body_md: A case search may emphasize published appellate decisions while omitting unreported lower-court outcomes, settlements or non-English sources. Those gaps can distort predictions about how often claims succeed. A sophisticated lawyer distinguishes the law expressed in controlling precedents from empirical claims about outcomes. The fact that a database contains many decisions of one kind is not proof every dispute ends that way. Research design must account for what was never recorded or indexed.

sections.title: Test the Unfavorable Hypothesis
sections.body_md: If early research suggests a defendant violated a duty, seek reliable facts and sources that would rebut that claim. This reduces motivated reasoning and exposes missing elements. The result may strengthen or weaken the client's case. Accurate advice needs both possibilities because it informs settlement, litigation and ethical choices. The researcher's credibility comes from trying to discover the truth under the applicable law, not from assembling the largest collection of favorable materials.

black.focus: Design research safeguards against systemic informational harm
black.summary: At doctoral depth, examine how flawed legal information systems can reproduce injustice at scale. Propose verifiable, privacy-respecting methods for legal research and communication.
checklist: I can analyze systemic risks of fabricated authority
I can design reproducible research review
I can evaluate unequal access to trustworthy legal information

sections.title: A Small Error Can Scale
sections.body_md: An automated legal database may repeat a mistaken summary across hundreds of answers, turning one flawed interpretation into routine advice. Systems that prioritize speed without verifying primary sources can magnify legal harm. The scholar's task is to specify failure modes: nonexistent cases, outdated statutes, mistranslations, omitted exceptions and unauthorized disclosure. Quality assurance should target each risk with traceable sources, version control and a process for reporting and correcting errors.

The scholar's task is to specify failure modes: nonexistent cases, outdated statutes, mistranslations, omitted exceptions and unauthorized disclosure. Quality assurance should target each risk with traceable sources, version control and a process for reporting and correcting errors.

sections.title: Correction Must Be Possible
sections.body_md: A trustworthy research system retains a minimal record showing which sources supported a material assertion, which version was used, and who reviewed it. Corrections should update dependent conclusions and alert affected users where necessary and lawful. At the same time, audit records must avoid unnecessary storage of confidential client information. The balance between reproducibility and privacy is not solved by collecting everything. A disciplined system preserves what reviewers genuinely need and protects what clients entrusted.

sections.title: Access Is a Justice Issue
sections.body_md: Commercial databases and specialist counsel can make authoritative law easier for well-resourced parties to find than for those without money. Public access to laws, accessible legal education and reliable low-cost research tools can reduce that disparity. Yet simplified advice can be dangerous if it conceals jurisdictional differences or limitations. A doctoral proposal must pair accessibility with source accuracy, clear warnings about uncertainty, and practical routes to qualified assistance when a person's life or liberty is at stake.
